# gh-dash TUI Design Overview

## Overall Layout & Structure

gh-dash implements a **sidebar + main content** layout pattern. The interface features:

- **Left sidebar**: Navigation between sections (PRs and Issues), with `ctrl+d/u` for movement
- **Main viewing area**: Tabular display of items organized by custom-defined sections
- **Section-based organization**: Users can define multiple filtered views (e.g., "My Pull Requests," "Needs My Review")

## Table/List View

The primary interface displays items in columnar format with:
- Configurable section visibility and item counts
- Optional row separators and compact/expanded modes
- Row-level navigation using vim keybindings (`h/j/k/l`)

## Keybindings & Navigation

Native vim-style controls include:
- **Movement**: `h/j/k/l` for rows and sections
- **Actions**: `o` (open in browser), `y/Y` (copy PR number/URL)
- **Sidebar**: `ctrl+d/u` for scrolling
- Additional command bindings available via help menu

## Theming & Styling

Customizable color schemes supporting:
- Primary and secondary text colors
- Multiple built-in themes (Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night)
- Border and separator styling options
- Configuration through YAML color definitions

## Configuration Model

Users define behavior through YAML:
- **Custom filters**: GitHub query syntax for PR/issue sections
- **Custom commands**: Mappable keyboard shortcuts executing shell commands with variable interpolation (`.RepoPath`, `.PrNumber`)
- **Theme settings**: UI colors, layout preferences

## Key Features

"A rich terminal UI for GitHub that doesn't break your flow" emphasizing native vim integration, custom filtering, and extensible command execution for GitHub workflow optimization.

# entire-judge — gh-dash-style jury dashboard TUI

## Context

The jury surface Thomas pitched from day one ("a TUI on the side with metrics and quick
bullets") needs to become real. His latest ask: a TUI with **one page per submitted repo,
showing the scoring, a summary, and additional findings**, styled like
[gh-dash](https://www.gh-dash.dev/) — a sidebar list + per-item detail, vim keybinds,
bordered panes, themes, filter, and a help bar.

entire-judge already has a minimal two-pane bubbletea TUI (`internal/tui/tui.go`, 202 lines:
left submission list ↔ right detail with per-lens score bars + verdicts + bullets, expand
evidence with `enter`). It's ~60% of the way there. The gaps: **no holistic summary**, **no
dedicated findings block** (the rich `Metrics` go unused in the TUI), and **no gh-dash
polish** (no bordered panes, columns, scrolling, tabs, filter, themes, or help bar).

This plan rebuilds the TUI into a gh-dash-style dashboard and adds an LLM-written per-
submission summary (with a deterministic fallback so it never renders blank).

## Decisions (confirmed with user)
- **Summary = LLM-written** (one short agent call per submission), with a **composed
  deterministic fallback** when no agent is available (no-egress / agent down) so the
  Summary section is never empty.
- **Full gh-dash treatment**: ranked table + scrollable per-repo page (Score / Summary /
  Findings) + an Excluded (hard-gated) section + vim+arrow nav + help bar + `/` fuzzy
  filter + selectable color themes.
- **No new dependencies** — `bubbles` v1.0.0 (already required) ships `table`, `viewport`,
  `help`, `key`, `textinput`; verified present in the module cache.

## Data available (already on the report — `internal/judge/model.go`)
The TUI receives `[]judge.RunReport`. Each carries everything the three sections need:
- **Score**: `Composite`, `Flags`, and `Lenses[]` (`Lens`, `Score`, `Verdict`, `Bullets`,
  `Evidence`, `Supported`).
- **Findings**: `Deterministic Metrics` — timeline category/reason, sessions/turns/human
  prompts/files/facts/checkpoints, tokens (in/out/cache), commit coverage
  (total/pre/covered/missing/no-history/merge), session timestamps, time-on-task, first-
  commit↔first-session delta, `AgentHistogram`, `PrimaryAgent`. Plus per-lens bullets +
  evidence anchors and `Warnings`.
- **Header**: `SubmissionID`, `RepoDir`, `BrainPath`, `Run` (agent/model/fingerprint/
  hackathon start/llm status).
No new metrics needed; only a new `Summary` string field (below).

## LLM summary (`internal/judge`)
- **Schema**: add `Summary string \`json:"summary,omitempty"\`` to `RunReport`
  (`model.go`). Additive — existing JSON consumers unaffected.
- **New template** `templates/entire-judge-summary.md` — auto-embedded by the existing
  `//go:embed templates/*.md` (`templates.go`); no embed change. Prompt: write a 2–3
  sentence, evidence-grounded overview of *what the team built and how it went*; forbid
  inventing numbers (same anti-fabrication rule as the lenses); output one JSON object
  `{"summary":"…"}`.
- **Generation** (`submission.go`, after the lenses in `Submit`): `runSummary(ctx, sc,
  params, run) (string, error)` reusing the existing lens plumbing — `renderTemplate` →
  `agent.CommandArgs`/`InjectModel`/`InjectEffort` → the run `agent.Runner` → lenient JSON
  parse (mirror `runLens`/`parseLensOutput` in `lens.go`). On success set `report.Summary`;
  on error append a warning and leave it empty (degrade like the other LLM lenses; this is
  the +1 call/submission the user opted into).
- **Deterministic fallback** `ComposeSummary(RunReport) string` (`internal/judge/summary.go`):
  stitches timeline category + the idea/plan/execution and prompting verdicts + headline
  metrics (sessions/files/time-on-task) into one line. Used by the TUI and the plain
  renderer whenever `report.Summary == ""`.

## TUI architecture (`internal/tui/`, package `tui`)
Rewrite the package into focused files (root model + renderers + theme):
- `tui.go` — root bubbletea `Model` (bubbletea), `Update`, `View`, window sizing, focus
  model, key dispatch. Composes the sub-components below.
- `styles.go` — **theme registry** (`default`, `catppuccin`, `gruvbox`, `tokyonight`): each
  a struct of lipgloss colors (border, accent, dim, text, score good/ok/bad, flag pill).
  `ThemeByName(string) Theme`, default dark. Selected via a new `--theme` flag (and
  `ENTIRE_JUDGE_THEME` env fallback).
- `table.go` — build a `bubbles/table` for the ranked list. Columns: **Rank · Submission ·
  Score · Flags** (single-line rows; flags truncated). A second table/section for the
  **Excluded (hard-gated)** submissions.
- `detail.go` — render the selected submission's page into a `bubbles/viewport`:
  1. **Header** — submission id, repo, agent/model, LLM status, hackathon start, big composite.
  2. **Score** — per-lens colored bars (`authenticity`, `idea_plan_execution`,
     `prompting_skill`, `effort_consistency`) with weights, `agent_leverage` descriptive
     line, and flags (e.g. `prompting_skill_unsupported`).
  3. **Summary** — `report.Summary` (LLM) or `ComposeSummary` fallback.
  4. **Findings** — a deterministic metrics block (sessions/turns/prompts/files/time-on-
     task/tokens, commit coverage, first-commit↔first-session delta, agent mix) + each
     lens's bullets + evidence anchors + warnings.
- `filter.go` — `/` opens a `bubbles/textinput`; filters table rows by submission id
  (substring/fuzzy); `esc` closes.
- `keys.go` — `bubbles/key` `key.Map` + `bubbles/help` short/full help (`?` toggles).

**Components reused** (`bubbles` v1.0.0): `table.New(opts...)` (list, scroll, focus),
`viewport.New(w,h)` (scroll detail; `ctrl+d/u`, `pgup/pgdn`), `help.New()`+`key`
(help bar), `textinput.New()` (filter).

**Layout** (gh-dash sidebar+main): top title bar (`entire-judge — N submissions · agent ·
hackathon start`); body = left bordered pane (~1/3 width, min 28) holding the section tabs
**Ranked (N) | Excluded (M)** + the active table, right bordered pane (~2/3) holding the
detail viewport; footer = short help + the advisory `Disclaimer`. Borders/colors from the
theme.

**Focus & keys** (vim + arrows, gh-dash-like): `↑/k`,`↓/j` move selection (detail auto-
updates — gh-dash preview behavior); `→/l/enter` focus detail; `←/h/esc` back to list (or
close filter); `ctrl+d/u`,`pgup/pgdn` scroll detail; `tab`/`shift-tab` (or `1`/`2`) switch
Ranked↔Excluded; `/` filter; `?` help; `q`/`ctrl+c` quit.

## Wiring (`internal/cli/commands.go`)
- **Pass excluded reports to the TUI.** In `runJudgeRank`, keep each hard-gated
  submission's full `RunReport` (today only `RankExcluded{ID,BrainPath,Reason}` is kept for
  JSON — leave that unchanged) and hand both ranked + excluded report slices to the TUI.
  Change `runTUI(cmd, reports, meta)` → `runTUI(cmd, ranked, excluded, theme, meta)`; `run`
  (single submission) passes `excluded=nil`.
- **`--theme` flag** in `registerRunFlags` (shared by run/rank/watch); resolve
  `ThemeByName` with `ENTIRE_JUDGE_THEME` fallback.
- **Plain output** (`printRunReport`): add a `Summary:` line (`report.Summary` or
  `ComposeSummary`). `printRankReport` stays score-focused. Non-TTY `--plain`/`--json`
  behavior unchanged; `ScoreBar` stays plain text (TUI does its own colored bar so no ANSI
  leaks into `--plain`).

## Critical files to reuse
- `internal/judge/lens.go` — `runLens`, `renderTemplate`, `parseLensOutput`,
  `validateEvidenceAnchors` (clone the plumbing for `runSummary`).
- `internal/judge/submission.go` — `Submit` (add the summary call), `runScoredLens` pattern.
- `internal/judge/templates.go` — `//go:embed templates/*.md`, `loadTemplate`,
  `stripTemplateFrontmatter` (the summary template rides this for free).
- `internal/agent/agent.go` — `CommandArgs`/`InjectModel`/`InjectEffort`/`RejectForNoEgress`;
  `runner.go` `DefaultRunner` (the summary uses the same agent + no-egress gate as lenses).
- `internal/tui/tui.go` — keep `ScoreBar` exported (used by `printRunReport`); reuse the
  existing two-pane sizing/`JoinHorizontal` idea, the `Disclaimer` footer.
- `internal/cli/commands.go` — `commandOutputIsTTY`, `runTUI`, `registerRunFlags`,
  `printRunReport`.

## Verification
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` green. New
  unit tests: `ComposeSummary` (deterministic), summary template loads (extend
  `TestTemplatesLoad`), `runSummary` lenient-parse with a fake runner, and pure TUI helpers
  (table-row builder, filter match, detail-section formatter). Existing tests stay green
  (the `Summary` field is additive).
- **Live TTY** against the demo brains:
  `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR=/Users/suhaan/judge-demo/brains ./entire-judge rank
  /Users/suhaan/judge-demo --started-at 2026-05-28T09:00:00Z` → dashboard opens; verify the
  ranked table, selection→detail, Score/Summary/Findings render, viewport scroll, `tab`
  section switch, `/` filter, `--theme catppuccin`, `?` help, `q` quit. `watch` and
  single-repo `run` open the same dashboard (run = one-row table).
- **Excluded section**: add `entireio/cli` (predates_event) to a demo dir to confirm the
  Excluded tab lists it with its gate reason and a viewable detail page.
- **Non-TTY**: `rank … --plain` and `--json` unchanged; `run <repo> --plain` shows the
  `Summary:` line; with no agent (`--agent ollama` offline / no-egress) the Summary falls
  back to `ComposeSummary` rather than blank.
- All artifacts stay neutral (no person names in templates/code/commits).

# entire-judge — gh-dash-style jury dashboard TUI

## Context

The jury surface Thomas pitched from day one ("a TUI on the side with metrics and quick
bullets") needs to become real. His latest ask: a TUI with **one page per submitted repo,
showing the scoring, a summary, and additional findings**, styled like
[gh-dash](https://www.gh-dash.dev/) — a sidebar list + per-item detail, vim keybinds,
bordered panes, themes, filter, and a help bar.

entire-judge already has a minimal two-pane bubbletea TUI (`internal/tui/tui.go`, 202 lines:
left submission list ↔ right detail with per-lens score bars + verdicts + bullets, expand
evidence with `enter`). It's ~60% of the way there. The gaps: **no holistic summary**, **no
dedicated findings block** (the rich `Metrics` go unused in the TUI), and **no gh-dash
polish** (no bordered panes, columns, scrolling, tabs, filter, themes, or help bar).

This plan rebuilds the TUI into a gh-dash-style dashboard and adds an LLM-written per-
submission summary (with a deterministic fallback so it never renders blank).

## Decisions (confirmed with user)
- **Summary = LLM-written** (one short agent call per submission), with a **composed
  deterministic fallback** when no agent is available (no-egress / agent down) so the
  Summary section is never empty.
- **Full gh-dash treatment**: ranked table + scrollable per-repo page (Score / Summary /
  Findings) + an Excluded (hard-gated) section + vim+arrow nav + help bar + `/` fuzzy
  filter + selectable color themes.
- **No new dependencies** — `bubbles` v1.0.0 (already required) ships `table`, `viewport`,
  `help`, `key`, `textinput`; verified present in the module cache.

## Data available (already on the report — `internal/judge/model.go`)
The TUI receives `[]judge.RunReport`. Each carries everything the three sections need:
- **Score**: `Composite`, `Flags`, and `Lenses[]` (`Lens`, `Score`, `Verdict`, `Bullets`,
  `Evidence`, `Supported`).
- **Findings**: `Deterministic Metrics` — timeline category/reason, sessions/turns/human
  prompts/files/facts/checkpoints, tokens (in/out/cache), commit coverage
  (total/pre/covered/missing/no-history/merge), session timestamps, time-on-task, first-
  commit↔first-session delta, `AgentHistogram`, `PrimaryAgent`. Plus per-lens bullets +
  evidence anchors and `Warnings`.
- **Header**: `SubmissionID`, `RepoDir`, `BrainPath`, `Run` (agent/model/fingerprint/
  hackathon start/llm status).
No new metrics needed; only a new `Summary` string field (below).

## LLM summary (`internal/judge`)
- **Schema**: add `Summary string` (`json:"summary,omitempty"`) to `RunReport`
  (`model.go`). Additive — existing JSON consumers unaffected.
- **New template** `templates/entire-judge-summary.md` — auto-embedded by the existing
  `//go:embed templates/*.md` (`templates.go`); no embed change. Prompt: write a 2–3
  sentence, evidence-grounded overview of *what the team built and how it went*; forbid
  inventing numbers (same anti-fabrication rule as the lenses); output one JSON object
  `{"summary":"…"}`.
- **Generation** (`submission.go`, after the lenses in `Submit`): `runSummary(ctx, sc,
  params, run) (string, error)` reusing the existing lens plumbing — `renderTemplate` →
  `agent.CommandArgs`/`InjectModel`/`InjectEffort` → the run `agent.Runner` → lenient JSON
  parse (mirror `runLens`/`parseLensOutput` in `lens.go`). On success set `report.Summary`;
  on error append a warning and leave it empty (degrade like the other LLM lenses; this is
  the +1 call/submission the user opted into).
- **Deterministic fallback** `ComposeSummary(RunReport) string` (`internal/judge/summary.go`):
  stitches timeline category + the idea/plan/execution and prompting verdicts + headline
  metrics (sessions/files/time-on-task) into one line. Used by the TUI and the plain
  renderer whenever `report.Summary == ""`.

## TUI architecture (`internal/tui/`, package `tui`)
Rewrite the package into focused files (root model + renderers + theme):
- `tui.go` — root bubbletea `Model`, `Update`, `View`, window sizing, focus model, key
  dispatch. Composes the sub-components below.
- `styles.go` — **theme registry** (`default`, `catppuccin`, `gruvbox`, `tokyonight`): each
  a struct of lipgloss colors (border, accent, dim, text, score good/ok/bad, flag pill).
  `ThemeByName(string) Theme`, default dark. Selected via a new `--theme` flag (and
  `ENTIRE_JUDGE_THEME` env fallback).
- `table.go` — build a `bubbles/table` for the ranked list. Columns: **Rank · Submission ·
  Score · Flags** (single-line rows; flags truncated). A second table/section for the
  **Excluded (hard-gated)** submissions.
- `detail.go` — render the selected submission's page into a `bubbles/viewport`:
  1. **Header** — submission id, repo, agent/model, LLM status, hackathon start, big composite.
  2. **Score** — per-lens colored bars (`authenticity`, `idea_plan_execution`,
     `prompting_skill`, `effort_consistency`) with weights, `agent_leverage` descriptive
     line, and flags (e.g. `prompting_skill_unsupported`).
  3. **Summary** — `report.Summary` (LLM) or `ComposeSummary` fallback.
  4. **Findings** — a deterministic metrics block (sessions/turns/prompts/files/time-on-
     task/tokens, commit coverage, first-commit↔first-session delta, agent mix) + each
     lens's bullets + evidence anchors + warnings.
- `filter.go` — `/` opens a `bubbles/textinput`; filters table rows by submission id
  (substring/fuzzy); `esc` closes.
- `keys.go` — `bubbles/key` `key.Map` + `bubbles/help` short/full help (`?` toggles).

**Components reused** (`bubbles` v1.0.0): `table.New(opts...)` (list, scroll, focus),
`viewport.New(w,h)` (scroll detail; `ctrl+d/u`, `pgup/pgdn`), `help.New()`+`key`
(help bar), `textinput.New()` (filter).

**Layout** (gh-dash sidebar+main): top title bar (`entire-judge — N submissions · agent ·
hackathon start`); body = left bordered pane (~1/3 width, min 28) holding the section tabs
**Ranked (N) | Excluded (M)** + the active table, right bordered pane (~2/3) holding the
detail viewport; footer = short help + the advisory `Disclaimer`. Borders/colors from the
theme.

**Focus & keys** (vim + arrows, gh-dash-like): `↑/k`,`↓/j` move selection (detail auto-
updates — gh-dash preview behavior); `→/l/enter` focus detail; `←/h/esc` back to list (or
close filter); `ctrl+d/u`,`pgup/pgdn` scroll detail; `tab`/`shift-tab` (or `1`/`2`) switch
Ranked↔Excluded; `/` filter; `?` help; `q`/`ctrl+c` quit.

## Wiring (`internal/cli/commands.go`)
- **Pass excluded reports to the TUI.** In `runJudgeRank`, keep each hard-gated
  submission's full `RunReport` (today only `RankExcluded{ID,BrainPath,Reason}` is kept for
  JSON — leave that unchanged) and hand both ranked + excluded report slices to the TUI.
  Change `runTUI(cmd, reports, meta)` → `runTUI(cmd, ranked, excluded, theme, meta)`; `run`
  (single submission) passes `excluded=nil`.
- **`--theme` flag** in `registerRunFlags` (shared by run/rank/watch); resolve
  `ThemeByName` with `ENTIRE_JUDGE_THEME` fallback.
- **Plain output** (`printRunReport`): add a `Summary:` line (`report.Summary` or
  `ComposeSummary`). `printRankReport` stays score-focused. Non-TTY `--plain`/`--json`
  behavior unchanged; `ScoreBar` stays plain text (TUI does its own colored bar so no ANSI
  leaks into `--plain`).

## Critical files to reuse
- `internal/judge/lens.go` — `runLens`, `renderTemplate`, `parseLensOutput`,
  `validateEvidenceAnchors` (clone the plumbing for `runSummary`).
- `internal/judge/submission.go` — `Submit` (add the summary call), `runScoredLens` pattern.
- `internal/judge/templates.go` — `//go:embed templates/*.md`, `loadTemplate`,
  `stripTemplateFrontmatter` (the summary template rides this for free).
- `internal/agent/agent.go` — `CommandArgs`/`InjectModel`/`InjectEffort`/`RejectForNoEgress`;
  `runner.go` `DefaultRunner` (the summary uses the same agent + no-egress gate as lenses).
- `internal/tui/tui.go` — keep `ScoreBar` exported (used by `printRunReport`); reuse the
  existing two-pane sizing/`JoinHorizontal` idea, the `Disclaimer` footer.
- `internal/cli/commands.go` — `commandOutputIsTTY`, `runTUI`, `registerRunFlags`,
  `printRunReport`.

## Verification
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` green. New
  unit tests: `ComposeSummary` (deterministic), summary template loads (extend
  `TestTemplatesLoad`), `runSummary` lenient-parse with a fake runner, and pure TUI helpers
  (table-row builder, filter match, detail-section formatter). Existing tests stay green
  (the `Summary` field is additive).
- **Live TTY** against the demo brains:
  `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR=/Users/suhaan/judge-demo/brains ./entire-judge rank
  /Users/suhaan/judge-demo --started-at 2026-05-28T09:00:00Z` → dashboard opens; verify the
  ranked table, selection→detail, Score/Summary/Findings render, viewport scroll, `tab`
  section switch, `/` filter, `--theme catppuccin`, `?` help, `q` quit. `watch` and
  single-repo `run` open the same dashboard (run = one-row table).
- **Excluded section**: add `entireio/cli` (predates_event) to a demo dir to confirm the
  Excluded tab lists it with its gate reason and a viewable detail page.
- **Non-TTY**: `rank … --plain` and `--json` unchanged; `run <repo> --plain` shows the
  `Summary:` line; with no agent (`--agent ollama` offline / no-egress) the Summary falls
  back to `ComposeSummary` rather than blank.
- All artifacts stay neutral (no person names in templates/code/commits).

**Yes — entire-brain uses entire-sem (this is the opposite of entire-judge).**

I verified it in entire-brain's production code:
- During `entire brain refresh`, the semantic-index step shells out to the sem plugin: `entire sem doctor --json` (`semantic.go:738`) and `entire sem snapshot --repo <dir> --format ndjson --no-network` (`semantic.go:771`).
- The resulting records are stored in the brain with `Provider = "entire-sem"` (`semantic.go:390`), and `refresh.go` even exposes a `--sem-binary` flag for it.
- It's a **graceful/optional** provider (`--no-network`, degrades if sem isn't installed) — `regression.go:1191` calls it "the graceful upgrade entire-brain gets from entire-sem."

So the full picture, cleanly:

| | uses entire-sem? | how |
|---|---|---|
| **entire-brain** | **Yes** | calls `entire sem snapshot`/`doctor` during `refresh` to add a code-structure layer (symbols, routes, tools, workflows) to the brain |
| **entire-judge** | **No** | reads the brain's sessions, prompts, facts, and git history directly |

The useful implication: because the **brain already contains a sem-derived semantic layer** (when refresh ran with sem available), if we ever want the judge to use code-structure for an "execution" signal, it can just **read that existing layer out of the brain** — no need to couple the judge to the sem plugin at all. Cleaner than what I floated earlier.

**Tighter answer for Thomas:**
> entire-brain *does* use sem — during `refresh` it calls `entire sem snapshot` to add a code-structure layer (symbols/routes/tools) to the brain, as an optional provider. The judge just doesn't read that particular layer yet; it uses the sessions, prompts, facts, and commit history. So if we want code-level execution signal in the judge later, it can read sem's data straight out of the brain rather than calling sem itself.

content.text:
Verified against the code. Here's the precise answer to **"does it use entire-sem *through* the brain?"** — **No, not in any real sense:**

The judge's brain reader (`internal/brainstore/store.go`) reads exactly three things from the brain — `manifest.json`, the session transcripts, and `facts.ndjson` — plus it runs `git` directly for commit history. Crucially:
- The **durable facts** it reads are produced by `entire brain distill` (an LLM pass over the *sessions*), **not** by sem.
- The **sem-derived semantic snapshot** that `refresh` builds lives in a separate `snapshots/` store that the judge **never opens**.

So even though the brain *contains* a sem layer, the judge consumes a different slice of it (sessions, prompts, distilled facts, git history). The only "sem" mentions in the judge's code are two comments noting it's *structurally modeled after* sem — zero data dependency.

**So "uses the brain, not sem" is accurate even accounting for the indirection.** For Thomas:
> Right — the brain *can* hold a sem-built semantic layer, but the judge doesn't read it. It uses the sessions, prompts, distilled facts, and commit history. The facts come from distill (LLM over sessions), not from sem. So no sem, directly or through the brain.

## Usage reporting

Regente only displays real usage reported by a real joined agent. Never estimate, infer, or invent token/context numbers.

## Adding submissions

`entire judge add <repo-url>` readies a submission end to end: it clones the repo
into `--dir` (default `.`), fetches its Entire checkpoint history
(`refs/heads/entire/*`), and builds the brain by shelling out to
`entire brain refresh sessions` (override the binary with `--entire-binary`, or
pass `--build=false` to clone only). Point `rank`/`watch` at the directory of
added submissions to score them all.

```sh
entire judge add https://github.com/team/project --dir ./submissions
entire judge rank ./submissions --started-at <event-start>
```

## entire-sem (the execution signal)

`entire judge` reads the brain directly; it does **not** call entire-sem. But when
a brain was built with the sem provider (`entire brain refresh` records a
`sources.semantic` layer), the judge reads that snapshot straight from the brain
and feeds a "What was built" digest (symbol kinds, capabilities, busiest files)
into the **idea_plan_execution** lens — turning execution scoring from coarse
file/commit counts into a built-vs-planned comparison. Brains without a sem layer
score exactly as before.

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Visual questions ahead?";
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [label="yes"];
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Ask clarifying questions" [label="no"];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion:** When you anticipate that upcoming questions will involve visual content (mockups, layouts, diagrams), offer it once for consent:
> "Some of what we're working on might be easier to explain if I can show it to you in a web browser. I can put together mockups, diagrams, comparisons, and other visuals as we go. This feature is still new and can be token-intensive. Want to try it? (Requires opening a local URL)"

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Do not combine it with clarifying questions, context summaries, or any other content. The message should contain ONLY the offer above and nothing else. Wait for the user's response before continuing. If they decline, proceed with text-only brainstorming.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:

Find and report (with exact file paths and line numbers):

1. The CLI entry point(s): main.go / cmd packages. What command framework is used (cobra? urfave/cli? stdlib flag?). List every top-level command and subcommand (e.g. `brain refresh`, `brain refresh sessions`, `brain refresh index`, anything like `show`, `list`, `inspect`, `search`, `status`, `doctor`, `query`). For each, one line on what it does.

2. How output is currently presented to the user for each command: plain text? JSON? a table? Is there ANY existing interactive/TUI code anywhere (search for "bubbletea", "charmbracelet", "lipgloss", "bubbles", "tea.", "tview", "termui", "tcell")? Report whether any TUI exists at all today.

input.description: Map entire-brain data model
input.prompt:
Explore the Go repository at /Users/suhaan/Documents/Coding/entire-brain (the "entire-brain" plugin — it builds a local "brain" from knowledge sources). I need a thorough map of the **brain's data model and on-disk layout**, because we may build a TUI dashboard that displays brain contents, and I need to know exactly what data exists to show.

Find and report (with exact file paths and line numbers):

1. The "brain" is built from ~4 knowledge sources (commonly: sessions, seed, semantic, history). Find the data model / Go structs for the brain manifest and each source. What is the manifest structure (e.g. a `manifest.json` schema / a `Manifest` struct)? What does each source contribute and what fields does each record carry? Look in packages likely named brainstore, store, brain, manifest, index, semantic, sessions, history, facts, seed.

2. The on-disk layout of a built brain: directory structure (e.g. `<brain>/repos/gh/<owner>/<repo>/manifest.json`, `semantic/snapshots/...`, sessions files, facts files). Map the directories and the key files in each, and what each file contains.

3. What individual "entries" or "records" look like that a dashboard could list and show detail for — e.g. sessions (with turns/prompts/timestamps/agents), facts, semantic symbols/relations, history/checkpoints/commits. Show the relevant struct definitions with their fields.

4. Any summary/aggregate statistics already computed about a brain (counts of sessions, facts, symbols, files, commits; provider info; capabilities; timestamps). Where are these computed and stored? Show the struct(s).

5. How the semantic layer integrates (the `entire sem` snapshot — NDJSON records with record_type symbol/relation/file, kind, name, file_path, language). Where is it loaded/parsed and into what structs?

Report as a structured summary with file:line references and the key struct definitions verbatim (just the structs, not whole files). Be thorough across internal/.

input.description: Map entire-judge TUI feature set
input.prompt:
Explore the Go repository at /Users/suhaan/Documents/Coding/entire-judge — specifically the `internal/tui/` package and how the CLI wires it up. I'm going to port this TUI experience to a different project, so I need an exact, complete inventory of "the full thing" — every feature, component, file, and dependency.

Report (with file paths and line numbers):

1. Every file in internal/tui/ and what it does: tui.go (root model/Update/View/resize/mouse/keys), table.go, styles.go (themes), detail.go, keys.go, and any filter.go or others. For each, list the key types and functions with signatures.

2. The full feature inventory of the dashboard, as a checklist a port must reproduce:
   - Two-pane gh-dash layout (left list + right detail), bordered panes, title bar, footer/help bar
   - Section tabs (e.g. Ranked / Excluded) and how switching works
   - The left table: columns, widths, centered rank column, trailing medal/flag mark column
   - The right detail page: which sections (Header, Score, Summary, Findings), what each renders
   - Themes: how many, names, the Theme struct fields, ThemeByName, env/flag selection
   - Filter (`/` textinput), help (`?`), vim+arrow nav, viewport scrolling
   - Clickable OSC8 links + the g/e keybindings that open URLs via the OS, openURLCmd/runtime.GOOS handling
   - Mouse click row selection (the Y-offset math, tableCapacity gating)
   - runewidth truncation, width clipping, medal()/rankColor helpers
   - LLM-written summary + deterministic ComposeSummary fallback (where it lives, internal/judge)

3. The exact external dependencies the TUI relies on: from go.mod, the versions of github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea, lipgloss, bubbles, github.com/mattn/go-runewidth, github.com/muesli/termenv. List them.

4. How the CLI command wires the TUI: the runTUI function signature, tea.WithMouseCellMotion, how ranked/excluded data + theme + metadata are passed in, the --theme flag, ENTIRE_JUDGE_THEME env fallback, and the non-TTY/--plain/--json fallback path.

5. The test files for the TUI (tui_test.go etc.) and what behaviors they lock in (so the port can carry equivalent tests).

Report as a structured, exhaustive summary with file:line references. Read the files to confirm specifics. The goal is a complete blueprint of what "porting the full thing" entails.

content.text:
I now have a clear picture of both sides:

- **entire-judge** "full thing" = a gh-dash two-pane TUI: left table + right detail page, section tabs, 4 themes, `/` filter, `?` help, vim/arrow/mouse nav, OSC8 clickable links + `g`/`e` openers, medals, runewidth-safe rendering, plus an LLM summary with deterministic fallback.
- **entire-brain** = a Cobra CLI plugin (`entire brain …`) with ~40 commands, **plain-text + JSON output only, no TUI today**, and a rich data model: a brain built from sources (sessions, semantic, history, facts, docs, seed), each with structured records (`factRecord`, `exportSession`, `semanticRecord`, `historyRecord`, `docRecord`) and aggregate stats per source.

So porting "the full thing" means building a brand-new `internal/tui/` package in entire-brain with the same gh-dash polish — but the central design fork is **what the dashboard browses**, since the brain has no "ranking" concept like judge did. Two things genuinely change the whole design, so let me confirm them before I write the plan.

questions.question: entire-judge's dashboard was a list of submissions → a detail page each. entire-brain has no ranking — it has a brain built from sources (facts, sessions, history, semantic, docs). What should the new `entire brain` dashboard primarily be?

options.label: Explorer w/ source tabs (Rec)
options.description: Direct port of the judge architecture: tabs across Facts / Sessions / History / Semantic; each tab is a browsable, filterable list; selecting an entry opens a rich detail page (the fact + provenance, the session's turns/summary, the symbol's signature/relations). Same two-pane + tabs + filter + themes + help layout.

options.label: Status & coverage dashboard
options.description: One page per knowledge source (sessions/semantic/history/facts/docs/seed) showing counts, freshness, coverage, blind spots, warnings. An interactive version of `brain status`/`overview` — a health view rather than an entry browser.

options.label: Combined (status home + explorer)
options.description: A 'home' status tab (source health/coverage) PLUS the explorer tabs that browse individual entries. The most complete, closest to 'the full thing' — but the largest build.

questions.question: entire-judge wrote an LLM summary per item (with a deterministic fallback). entire-brain is no-egress by default and its entries already carry text (fact text, session intent/outcome). How should each detail page's summary work?

options.label: Deterministic, no egress (Rec)
options.description: Compose each detail page from text the brain already stores (fact text + provenance, session intent/outcome, symbol signature). No agent calls — stays fully no-egress, the brain's default posture.

options.label: LLM summary like judge
options.description: Add an optional per-entry LLM-written summary behind a flag (deterministic fallback when off/unavailable). Matches entire-judge exactly but introduces egress and agent plumbing into the TUI path.

result.output: Your questions have been answered: "entire-judge's dashboard was a list of submissions → a detail page each. entire-brain has no ranking — it has a brain built from sources (facts, sessions, history, semantic, docs). What should the new `entire brain` dashboard primarily be?"="Combined (status home + explorer)", "entire-judge wrote an LLM summary per item (with a deterministic fallback). entire-brain is no-egress by default and its entries already carry text (fact text, session intent/outcome). How should each detail page's summary work?"="Deterministic, no egress (Rec)". You can now continue with these answers in mind.

content.text:
Decisions locked: **Combined dashboard** (status "home" tab + explorer tabs over entries) and **deterministic, no-egress** detail pages (render existing brain text — no agent calls). Both fit entire-brain's posture well.

The key engineering question now is how the TUI loads brain data read-only — I want to reuse entire-brain's existing loaders, not reinvent NDJSON/manifest parsing. Let me run two Plan agents in parallel: one to nail down the data-access reuse, one to design the TUI package + command wiring.

input.description: Design brain data-access for TUI
input.prompt:
You are designing the **read-only data-access layer** for a new interactive TUI dashboard in the Go repo at /Users/suhaan/Documents/Coding/entire-brain (the "entire-brain" plugin, module github.com/ashtom/entire-brain, package internal/cli, Cobra-based, go 1.26).

GOAL: A new `entire brain dash` TUI will show (a) a "home" status/coverage view of the brain's sources, and (b) explorer tabs that browse individual entries — **Facts, Sessions, History, Semantic** — with a detail page per entry. The TUI must be **no-egress and read-only** (no agent calls, no writes). I need you to find the EXISTING functions/loaders the TUI should reuse to load this data from a built brain on disk, so we don't reinvent parsing.

CONTEXT (already mapped — verify and go deeper):
- Brain manifest: `<brain>/manifest.json` (schema v3). Struct `exportManifest` in internal/cli/export.go ~2571; `brainSources` in internal/cli/brain.go ~20 (Seed/Sessions/Semantic/History/Facts/Docs source manifests).
- Per-source aggregate manifests carry counts/stats: `sessionSourceManifest` (brain.go ~29), `semanticSourceManifest` (semantic.go ~59), `historySourceManifest` (history.go ~51), `factSourceManifest` (facts.go ~42), `docSourceManifest` (doc.go ~29), `seedSourceManifest` (seed.go ~67).
- Entry records on disk: `factRecord` (facts.go ~85, in facts/<branch>/facts.ndjson), `exportSession` (export.go ~2595, in manifest sources.sessions + sessions/*.jsonl), `semanticRecord` (semantic.go ~133, in semantic/snapshots/<id>/snapshot.ndjson), `historyRecord` (history.go ~70, in history/index.json), `docRecord` (doc.go ~29).
- Status/overview already aggregate this: `brainStatusReport` (agent_surface.go ~53), `brainOverviewReport` (agent_surface.go ~217), and renderers `renderBrainOverviewText` (~377). The `status` command is at agent_surface.go ~201; `overview` ~244.
- Retrieval commands: `search`/`vsearch`/`query`/`get`/`multi-get` in retrieve_cmd.go; `recall` in facts_read_cmd.go ~38; `inspect code/context/impact/changes/tests` and `show` in agent_surface.go.

YOUR TASKS — report with exact file:line references and function signatures:
1. **Brain location**: How does code locate the brain directory for the current repo (the `path` command / a resolver func)? What function returns the brain dir + repo key? Trace it.
2. **Manifest load**: The exact function(s) that read & unmarshal `manifest.json` into `exportManifest`/`brainSources`. Signature + file:line. Can the TUI call it directly?
3. **Per-source entry loaders** — for EACH of Facts, Sessions, History, Semantic: the existing function that reads the entries into Go structs (e.g. a function that loads facts.ndjson → []factRecord; loads history/index.json → historyIndex; parses snapshot.ndjson → []semanticRecord; gets sessions from the manifest). Give signatures + file:line. Note which are exported vs unexported (the TUI is a new internal package; unexported funcs in internal/cli would need either to live in internal/cli too, or be promoted/wrapped).
4. **Status/coverage aggregates**: The function that builds `brainStatusReport` (for the home view) — signature + file:line — and whether it's reusable read-only. Same for overview.
5. **Detail-page data per entry type** (deterministic, no egress): for a selected fact, session, history record, semantic symbol — what's already loadable to populate a rich detail page? (e.g. fact: text+kind+paths+provenance anchors+related; session: agent/model/created/files/token usage/summary intent+outcome; semantic symbol: name/kind/qualified name/file:line/signature/language + its relations; history: kind/summary/path+line). Confirm the fields and where to read them.
6. **Recommended data-access design**: Given the TUI is a new package, recommend WHERE it should live and HOW it should access this data. Specifically evaluate: (A) put the TUI package as `internal/tui` and add a small read-only "brain reader" facade in internal/cli (or a new internal/brainview package) that the cli command calls to assemble a snapshot struct, passing plain data structs into the TUI (mirroring how entire-judge passed []RunReport into its tui package); vs (B) TUI imports internal/cli directly. Recommend the cleaner option and define the snapshot/data structs the TUI would receive. Flag any import-cycle or encapsulation risks.
7. **Edge cases**: missing brain (not built yet), empty sources, very large sources (thousands of facts/symbols — does anything stream or must we cap/paginate?), multi-branch facts (facts are per-branch), workspace vs single-repo brains. Note how to handle each read-only.

Be concrete and exhaustive. The output is a data-access blueprint another engineer will implement against. Read the files to confirm signatures; cite file:line everywhere.

input.description: Design TUI package + command wiring
input.prompt:
You are designing a new interactive TUI package for the Go repo at /Users/suhaan/Documents/Coding/entire-brain (module github.com/ashtom/entire-brain, Cobra CLI, go 1.26, package internal/cli). NO TUI exists today (output is plain-text + JSON only; no charmbracelet deps in go.mod).

We are PORTING the polished gh-dash-style TUI from a sibling repo at /Users/suhaan/Documents/Coding/entire-judge (its `internal/tui/` package) into entire-brain, adapted to the brain's data. Study /Users/suhaan/Documents/Coding/entire-judge/internal/tui/*.go (tui.go, table.go, detail.go, styles.go, keys.go) and its tui_test.go as the reference implementation to mirror.

PRODUCT DECISIONS (already made with the user):
- The dashboard is **Combined**: a "Home" status/coverage tab (per-source health: counts, freshness, coverage, blind spots, warnings) PLUS explorer tabs that browse individual entries — **Facts, Sessions, History, Semantic**. Selecting an entry opens a rich detail page.
- Detail pages are **deterministic and no-egress**: render text the brain already stores (fact text + kind + taxonomy paths + provenance anchors; session agent/model/created/files/token-usage/summary intent+outcome; semantic symbol name/kind/qualified-name/file:line/signature/language + relations; history kind/summary/path:line). NO agent calls anywhere in the TUI path.

PORT THESE FEATURES (the "full thing", same detail as entire-judge):
- Two-pane bordered layout (left list + right detail viewport), title bar, footer/help bar.
- Section tabs — here: Home | Facts | Sessions | History | Semantic — switch via tab/shift-tab (and maybe number keys); cursor resets, list rebuilds, detail refreshes.
- Left table (bubbles/table): per-tab columns appropriate to the entry type (e.g. Facts: kind · text-preview · status; Sessions: date · agent · files · session-id; Semantic: kind · name · file; History: kind · summary). Centered/aligned columns, runewidth-safe truncation.
- Right detail page: per-entry-type renderer (analogous to entire-judge's renderDetail) with section headers, color, deterministic content only.
- 4 themes ported verbatim (default/catppuccin/gruvbox/tokyonight), Theme struct, ThemeByName, --theme flag + an env fallback (use ENTIRE_BRAIN_THEME).
- `/` filter (textinput, case-insensitive substring over the visible list), `?` help (short/full), vim+arrow nav, viewport scroll, mouse wheel + click-to-select (reuse the Y-offset/tableCapacity approach), runewidth truncation, width clipping.
- Clickable links / openers adapted: instead of GitHub/entire.io, open the underlying SOURCE for the selected entry — e.g. a key to open the entry's file:line (semantic symbol's source file; fact/history transcript path) via the OS opener (runtime.GOOS → open/xdg-open/rundll32) and OSC8 links where a path/line exists. If no sensible target, omit.

YOUR TASKS — produce a file-by-file implementation blueprint:
1. **Package layout**: list every file to create under internal/tui/ (e.g. tui.go, model, table.go, detail.go, styles.go, keys.go, tabs, plus any per-entry detail renderer files) and what each contains. Define the root bubbletea Model struct fields (adapt entire-judge's Model: tabs/section, table, viewport, filter, help, theme, dimensions, focus, and the loaded brain data snapshot).
2. **Data interface**: define the plain data structs the TUI receives from the cli layer (a "brain snapshot": home/status summary + per-tab entry slices). The TUI must NOT do file IO itself — the cli command assembles the snapshot and passes it in (mirroring how entire-judge's runTUI passed []RunReport). Specify the struct shapes (fields per tab) that the detail renderers need; keep them decoupled from internal/cli structs (define TUI-local view models, or accept that a thin internal/brainview package owns them — recommend which).
3. **New command**: design `entire brain dash` (recommend this name; mention `tui`/`explore` as alternates) — where to register it (internal/cli/root.go EXPLORE group ~95-109), its flags (--theme, --json/--plain non-TTY fallback, maybe --tab to preselect, --branch for facts), and the runTUI wiring (tea.NewProgram with WithAltScreen + WithMouseCellMotion + WithOutput). Define the non-TTY fallback (print a plain status/overview + list, reusing existing renderers).
4. **go.mod additions**: exact modules+versions to add (charmbracelet/bubbletea v1.3.10, bubbles v1.0.0, lipgloss v1.1.0, mattn/go-runewidth, muesli/termenv) — confirm against entire-judge/go.mod, and note go.sum/vendoring implications for a go 1.26 module.
5. **Tests**: enumerate the unit tests to write mirroring entire-judge's tui_test.go (theme resolution, row builders per tab, detail renderer per entry type contains expected sections, View smoke test, click Y-offset, hyperlink zero-width, a JUDGE_DUMP-style dashboard snapshot env hook renamed appropriately). Pure, no-IO tests using small fixture structs.
6. **Risks & sequencing**: call out the hard parts (per-tab heterogeneous columns/rows in one bubbles/table, detail renderer dispatch by entry type, large lists/pagination, emoji/medal width — note medals likely irrelevant here so simpler, mouse Y-offset if tab bar adds a line). Give a build order (deps → styles/keys → data structs → table+detail per tab → model/update/view → command wiring → tests).

CONSTRAINT: No person's name (no "Thomas") anywhere in code, comments, command help, or test fixtures — keep all identifiers/strings neutral and product-focused.

Be concrete with Go signatures and file:line references to both repos. The output is a blueprint another engineer implements directly.

# entire-brain — gh-dash-style brain dashboard TUI (`entire brain dash`)

## Context

entire-brain today is a Cobra CLI plugin (`entire brain …`) with ~40 commands whose output is
**plain text + JSON only — there is no interactive UI**. The sibling project entire-judge grew a
polished gh-dash-style two-pane TUI (sidebar list ↔ per-item detail page, section tabs, themes,
`/` filter, `?` help, vim/arrow/mouse nav, clickable source links). The goal here is to bring that
same end-to-end experience to entire-brain, adapted to the brain's data model, so the brain becomes
**browsable and inspectable** interactively rather than only via one-shot commands.

Two product decisions are locked:
- **Combined dashboard**: a **Home** status/coverage tab (per-source health) PLUS explorer tabs that
  browse individual entries — **Facts, Sessions, History, Semantic** — each opening a rich detail page.
- **Deterministic, no-egress detail pages**: every page renders text the brain already stores. No agent
  calls anywhere in the TUI path — it stays read-only and preserves the brain's no-egress default.

Constraints: no person's name (e.g. "Thomas") in any code, comment, command help, test fixture, commit,
or PR — keep all strings neutral and product-focused. Do not push / open a PR without explicit review.

## Approach

Mirror entire-judge's clean split:
- A **pure `internal/tui` package** that imports nothing from `internal/cli` and only renders plain
  view-model structs handed to it (entire-judge passed `[]judge.RunReport`; here we pass a `tui.Snapshot`).
- A **new `internal/cli/dash.go`** command that resolves the brain, calls the existing (unexported)
  loaders to assemble the `tui.Snapshot`, resolves the theme, then launches the TUI on a TTY (or prints a
  plain/JSON fallback otherwise).

This one-directional dependency (`cli → tui`) avoids import cycles and matches the proven entire-judge layout.

### New package `internal/tui/` (pure rendering, ported from entire-judge `internal/tui/`)

- **`styles.go`** — `Theme` struct + 4 themes (`default`/`catppuccin`/`gruvbox`/`tokyonight`) ported verbatim,
  `ThemeByName`/`ThemeNames`/`normalizeThemeName`, style helpers (`titleStyle`/`dimStyle`/`textStyle`/
  `flagStyle`/`linkStyle`/`paneStyle`), `osc8`. Drop the ranking bits (medals/Gold/Silver/Bronze/rankColor);
  repurpose the score-band colors into **status colors** (fresh / stale / missing) used by the Home tab and
  fact-status coloring.
- **`keys.go`** — `keyMap` (Up/Down, Enter/→, Back/←/esc, Section=tab/shift+tab, Filter=`/`, **Open=`o`**,
  Help=`?`, Quit) + ShortHelp/FullHelp. Replaces judge's `g`/`e` GitHub openers with a single `o` = open the
  selected entry's underlying source.
- **`viewmodels.go`** — the plain structs the TUI consumes, decoupled from `internal/cli`:
  `Snapshot{ Repo, Branch, GeneratedAt, Home HomeView, Facts []FactView, Sessions []SessionView,
  History []HistoryView, Semantic []SemanticView, Notes []string }`; a `Tab` enum
  (`TabHome|TabFacts|TabSessions|TabHistory|TabSemantic`); and per-entry view models carrying exactly the
  deterministic fields a detail page needs (e.g. `FactView{Kind,Text,Paths,Status,Confidence,Provenance,RelatedIDs}`,
  `SessionView{ID,Agent,Model,CreatedAt,Files,Tokens,Intent,Outcome,TranscriptPath}`,
  `SemanticView{Kind,Name,QualifiedName,FilePath,StartLine,Signature,Language,Relations}`,
  `HistoryView{Kind,Summary,Path,Line}`, `HomeView{Sources []SourceHealth, Freshness, BlindSpots, Warnings}`).
- **`table.go`** — `columnsFor(tab, innerWidth)` + `rowsFor(tab, snapshot, filter)` with per-tab columns
  (Facts: kind · text-preview · status; Sessions: date · agent · files · id; Semantic: kind · name · file;
  History: kind · summary). runewidth-safe truncation (`truncate` via `runewidth.Truncate`).
- **`detail.go`** — `renderDetail(th, tab, entry, width)` dispatching to `renderHome`/`renderFact`/
  `renderSession`/`renderSemantic`/`renderHistory`, each with section headers and color, deterministic content
  only. Provenance/file paths rendered with OSC8 links where a target exists.
- **`tui.go`** — root bubbletea `Model` (adapt judge's: tabs/section, `table`, `viewport`, `filter`, `help`,
  `theme`, geometry, focus, `snapshot`), `Init/Update/View/resize/updateMouse/updateFiltering/rebuildVisible/
  refreshDetail/renderTabs/footerView`, an `openSource()` cmd (runtime.GOOS → open/xdg-open/rundll32 on a
  file:line or transcript path), and `func Run(snapshot Snapshot, theme Theme) error` building the program with
  `tea.WithAltScreen()`, `tea.WithMouseCellMotion()`, `tea.WithOutput(...)`. Mouse click row-select reuses
  judge's Y-offset/`tableCapacity` approach (recompute the first-data-row Y for this layout — the tab bar adds a
  line vs judge — and lock it with a test).
- **`tui_test.go`** — port/adapt judge's tests: theme resolution, per-tab row builders, each detail renderer
  contains its expected sections, `View` smoke test, click Y-offset, OSC8 zero-width width check, and a
  `BRAIN_DASH_DUMP`-gated ANSI-stripped snapshot dump. Pure, no IO, small fixture `Snapshot`.

### New command `internal/cli/dash.go`

- `newDashCommand(opts Options) *cobra.Command` registered in the **EXPLORE** group (root.go ~95–109).
  Name **`dash`** (alternates `tui`/`explore` if preferred). Flags: `--theme` (with `ENTIRE_BRAIN_THEME`
  env fallback), `--tab` (preselect), `--branch` (facts are per-branch), `--limit` (cap large lists),
  `--json`, `--plain`.
- `runDash(...)`: resolve repoDir + brainDir + branch via **`resolveFactsTarget`** (facts_read_cmd.go:14);
  if no brain, print the existing friendly not-built guidance. Assemble the snapshot, resolve theme, then:
  TTY → `tui.Run(snapshot, theme)`; non-TTY or `--plain` → reuse `renderBrainStatusText` + a plain list per
  tab; `--json` → marshal the snapshot via the existing `writeJSON` (workspace.go:1069).
- `assembleBrainSnapshot(ctx, opts, repoDir, brainDir, branch, limit) (tui.Snapshot, error)` — the only place
  that touches disk; maps existing cli structs → `tui` view-models by reusing:
  - **Home**: `buildBrainStatusReport` (agent_surface.go:1941) + `brainStatusBlindSpots`/
    `brainStatusFreshnessSeverity` (agent_surface.go:755–762).
  - **Facts**: `loadFacts(brainDir, branch)` (facts.go:208) → `[]factRecord`.
  - **History**: read `history/index.json` (history.go const `historyIndexPath`) into `historyIndex`
    (add a tiny `loadHistoryIndex` helper if none is already exported).
  - **Semantic**: parse `semantic/snapshots/<id>/snapshot.ndjson` (path from `semanticSourceManifest.SnapshotPath`)
    via the existing NDJSON record parsing in semantic.go → `[]semanticRecord` (symbols + relations).
  - **Sessions**: the manifest's `sources.sessions.Sessions` (`[]exportSession`) via the manifest unmarshal
    helper (export.go:543).
  Cap each list at `--limit` (default e.g. 500) and add a `Notes` line "showing N of M" so truncation is never silent.

### go.mod

Add (versions confirmed against entire-judge/go.mod, which builds this exact stack):
`github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea v1.3.10`, `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles v1.0.0`,
`github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss v1.1.0`, `github.com/mattn/go-runewidth v0.0.19`,
`github.com/muesli/termenv v0.16.0` (+ transitives). Run `go mod tidy`. go 1.26 module — `go get` resolves;
no vendoring in this repo.

## Critical files

- New: `internal/tui/{styles,keys,viewmodels,table,detail,tui,tui_test}.go`
- New: `internal/cli/dash.go` (+ `dash_test.go` for `assembleBrainSnapshot` against a tiny on-disk brain fixture,
  reusing fixture patterns from `facts_test.go` / `semantic_test.go`)
- Edit: `internal/cli/root.go` (register `dash` in EXPLORE group) and `go.mod` / `go.sum`
- Reference (port from): `/Users/suhaan/Documents/Coding/entire-judge/internal/tui/*.go` and its `tui_test.go`

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...` all green.
- Against a built brain (`entire brain refresh` on a real repo, or an existing brain in the data dir):
  `entire brain dash` opens the dashboard → Home shows per-source health/freshness/blind-spots; `tab` cycles
  Home → Facts → Sessions → History → Semantic; selecting an entry renders its deterministic detail page;
  `/` filters the list; `--theme catppuccin` restyles; `?` toggles help; `o` opens the entry's source
  (code file:line or transcript); `q` quits.
- Non-TTY: `entire brain dash --plain` prints status + per-tab lists; `--json` emits the snapshot; piping
  (non-TTY stdout) auto-falls back without a panic.
- Missing brain: prints the friendly "build it first" guidance, no crash.
- Confirm no agent/network calls occur in the dash path (grep the new code for runner/agent usage — should be none).

# entire-brain — gh-dash-style brain dashboard TUI (`entire brain dash`)

## Context

entire-brain today is a Cobra CLI plugin (`entire brain …`) with ~40 commands whose output is
**plain text + JSON only — there is no interactive UI**. The sibling project entire-judge grew a
polished gh-dash-style two-pane TUI (sidebar list ↔ per-item detail page, section tabs, themes,
`/` filter, `?` help, vim/arrow/mouse nav, clickable source links). The goal here is to bring that
same end-to-end experience to entire-brain, adapted to the brain's data model, so the brain becomes
**browsable and inspectable** interactively rather than only via one-shot commands.

Two product decisions are locked:
- **Combined dashboard**: a **Home** status/coverage tab (per-source health) PLUS explorer tabs that
  browse individual entries — **Facts, Sessions, History, Semantic** — each opening a rich detail page.
- **Deterministic, no-egress detail pages**: every page renders text the brain already stores. No agent
  calls anywhere in the TUI path — it stays read-only and preserves the brain's no-egress default.

Constraints: no person's name (e.g. "Thomas") in any code, comment, command help, test fixture, commit,
or PR — keep all strings neutral and product-focused. Do not push / open a PR without explicit review.

## Approach

Mirror entire-judge's clean split:
- A **pure `internal/tui` package** that imports nothing from `internal/cli` and only renders plain
  view-model structs handed to it (entire-judge passed `[]judge.RunReport`; here we pass a `tui.Snapshot`).
- A **new `internal/cli/dash.go`** command that resolves the brain, calls the existing (unexported)
  loaders to assemble the `tui.Snapshot`, resolves the theme, then launches the TUI on a TTY (or prints a
  plain/JSON fallback otherwise).

This one-directional dependency (`cli → tui`) avoids import cycles and matches the proven entire-judge layout.

### New package `internal/tui/` (pure rendering, ported from entire-judge `internal/tui/`)

- **`styles.go`** — `Theme` struct + 4 themes (`default`/`catppuccin`/`gruvbox`/`tokyonight`) ported verbatim,
  `ThemeByName`/`ThemeNames`/`normalizeThemeName`, style helpers (`titleStyle`/`dimStyle`/`textStyle`/
  `flagStyle`/`linkStyle`/`paneStyle`), `osc8`. Drop the ranking bits (medals/Gold/Silver/Bronze/rankColor);
  repurpose the score-band colors into **status colors** (fresh / stale / missing) used by the Home tab and
  fact-status coloring.
- **`keys.go`** — `keyMap` (Up/Down, Enter/→, Back/←/esc, Section=tab/shift+tab, Filter=`/`, **Open=`o`**,
  Help=`?`, Quit) + ShortHelp/FullHelp. Replaces judge's `g`/`e` GitHub openers with a single `o` = open the
  selected entry's underlying source.
- **`viewmodels.go`** — the plain structs the TUI consumes, decoupled from `internal/cli`:
  `Snapshot{ Repo, Branch, GeneratedAt, Home HomeView, Facts []FactView, Sessions []SessionView,
  History []HistoryView, Semantic []SemanticView, Notes []string }`; a `Tab` enum
  (`TabHome|TabFacts|TabSessions|TabHistory|TabSemantic`); and per-entry view models carrying exactly the
  deterministic fields a detail page needs (e.g. `FactView{Kind,Text,Paths,Status,Confidence,Provenance,RelatedIDs}`,
  `SessionView{ID,Agent,Model,CreatedAt,Files,Tokens,Intent,Outcome,TranscriptPath}`,
  `SemanticView{Kind,Name,QualifiedName,FilePath,StartLine,Signature,Language,Relations}`,
  `HistoryView{Kind,Summary,Path,Line}`, `HomeView{Sources []SourceHealth, Freshness, BlindSpots, Warnings}`).
- **`table.go`** — `columnsFor(tab, innerWidth)` + `rowsFor(tab, snapshot, filter)` with per-tab columns
  (Facts: kind · text-preview · status; Sessions: date · agent · files · id; Semantic: kind · name · file;
  History: kind · summary). runewidth-safe truncation (`truncate` via `runewidth.Truncate`).
- **`detail.go`** — `renderDetail(th, tab, entry, width)` dispatching to `renderHome`/`renderFact`/
  `renderSession`/`renderSemantic`/`renderHistory`, each with section headers and color, deterministic content
  only. Provenance/file paths rendered with OSC8 links where a target exists.
- **`tui.go`** — root bubbletea `Model` (adapt judge's: tabs/section, `table`, `viewport`, `filter`, `help`,
  `theme`, geometry, focus, `snapshot`), `Init/Update/View/resize/updateMouse/updateFiltering/rebuildVisible/
  refreshDetail/renderTabs/footerView`, an `openSource()` cmd (runtime.GOOS → open/xdg-open/rundll32 on a
  file:line or transcript path), and `func Run(snapshot Snapshot, theme Theme) error` building the program with
  `tea.WithAltScreen()`, `tea.WithMouseCellMotion()`, `tea.WithOutput(...)`. Mouse click row-select reuses
  judge's Y-offset/`tableCapacity` approach (recompute the first-data-row Y for this layout — the tab bar adds a
  line vs judge — and lock it with a test).
- **`tui_test.go`** — port/adapt judge's tests: theme resolution, per-tab row builders, each detail renderer
  contains its expected sections, `View` smoke test, click Y-offset, OSC8 zero-width width check, and a
  `BRAIN_DASH_DUMP`-gated ANSI-stripped snapshot dump. Pure, no IO, small fixture `Snapshot`.

120			if m.focusDetail {
121				if key.Matches(msg, m.keys.Back) {
122					m.focusDetail = false
123					return m, nil
124				}
125				var cmd tea.Cmd
126				m.vp, cmd = m.vp.Update(msg)
127				return m, cmd
128			}
129			// list focus
130			if key.Matches(msg, m.keys.Enter) {
131				if len(m.visible) > 0 {
132					m.focusDetail = true
133				}
134				return m, nil
135			}
136			prev := m.table.Cursor()
137			var cmd tea.Cmd
138			m.table, cmd = m.table.Update(msg)
139			if m.table.Cursor() != prev {
140				m.refreshDetail()
141			}
142			return m, cmd
143		}
144		return m, nil
145	}
146	
147	// updateMouse handles wheel scrolling (scrolls the detail page) and left-click
148	// (click a list row to open it, or click the detail pane to focus it). The chrome
149	// above the first list data row is: title(0) tabs(1) pane-top-border(2)
150	// header-text(3) header-bottom-border(4) first-row(5) — the bubbles/table header
151	// is two physical lines because of its bottom border. bubbles v1.0.0 exposes no
152	// scroll offset, so a click is only hit-tested when the whole list fits unscrolled
153	// (len <= tableCapacity); a scrolled list just focuses the page for the current
154	// selection rather than risk selecting the wrong row.
155	func (m Model) updateMouse(msg tea.MouseMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
156		if m.filtering {
157			return m, nil
158		}
159		if msg.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelUp || msg.Button == tea.MouseButtonWheelDown {
160			m.focusDetail = true
161			var cmd tea.Cmd
162			m.vp, cmd = m.vp.Update(msg)
163			return m, cmd
164		}
165		if msg.Action == tea.MouseActionPress && msg.Button == tea.MouseButtonLeft {
166			if msg.X >= m.leftTotal {
167				m.focusDetail = true
168				return m, nil
169			}
170			if row := msg.Y - 5; len(m.visible) <= m.tableCapacity && row >= 0 && row < len(m.visible) {
171				m.table.SetCursor(row)
172				m.refreshDetail()
173			}
174			m.focusDetail = true
175		}
176		return m, nil
177	}
178	
179	func (m Model) updateFiltering(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
180		switch msg.String() {
181		case "esc":
182			m.filtering = false
183			m.filter.Blur()
184			m.filter.SetValue("")
185			m.rebuildVisible()
186			return m, nil
187		case "enter":
188			m.filtering = false
189			m.filter.Blur()
190			return m, nil
191		}
192		var cmd tea.Cmd
193		m.filter, cmd = m.filter.Update(msg)
194		m.rebuildVisible()
195		return m, cmd
196	}
197	
198	// resize recomputes the pane geometry from the terminal size and re-flows the
199	// table, viewport, and detail content.
200	func (m *Model) resize() {
201		leftTotal := m.width / 3
202		if leftTotal < 30 {
203			leftTotal = 30
204		}
205		if leftTotal > 52 {
206			leftTotal = 52
207		}
208		rightTotal := m.width - leftTotal
209		m.leftTotal = leftTotal
210		m.leftInner = max(leftTotal-2, 12)
211		m.rightInner = max(rightTotal-2, 20)
212	
213		// Measure the footer's real height (the help line can wrap on a narrow
214		// terminal) so the body never overruns it — the source of the earlier
215		// content-cut-into-footer bug.
216		m.help.Width = m.width
217		footerH := lipgloss.Height(m.footerView())
218		bodyTotalH := m.height - 2 /*title+tabs*/ - footerH
219		if bodyTotalH < 8 {
220			bodyTotalH = 8
221		}
222		m.paneContentH = bodyTotalH - 2 // pane borders
223	
224		tableHeight := max(m.paneContentH-1, 3)
225		m.table.SetColumns(submissionColumns(m.leftInner))
226		m.table.SetWidth(m.leftInner)
227		m.table.SetHeight(tableHeight)
228		// Data rows shown = table height minus the 2-line header (text + bottom
229		// border). Used to decide whether a click can be safely hit-tested.
230		m.tableCapacity = max(tableHeight-2, 0)
231	
232		m.vp.Width = m.rightInner
233		m.vp.Height = m.paneContentH
234		m.filter.Width = m.leftInner - len(m.filter.Prompt) - 1
235		m.detailWidth = m.rightInner
236		m.refreshDetail()
237	}
238	
239	// selectedReport returns the report under the cursor in the active section, or
240	// nil when the section is empty.
241	func (m Model) selectedReport() *judge.RunReport {
242		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
243			return nil
244		}
245		idx := m.table.Cursor()
246		if idx < 0 || idx >= len(m.visible) {
247			return nil
248		}
249		return &m.visible[idx]
250	}
251	
252	// openSelected opens the selected submission's GitHub or entire.io page in the
253	// browser via the OS opener. This is the reliable path: with mouse capture on,
254	// terminals can't deliver plain clicks to the OSC 8 links, so the keybindings
255	// (g / e) drive navigation regardless of terminal support.
256	func (m Model) openSelected(which string) tea.Cmd {
257		r := m.selectedReport()
258		if r == nil {
259			return nil
260		}
261		owner, repo := ownerRepo(r.SubmissionID)
262		if owner == "" {
263			return nil
264		}
265		url := "https://entire.io/gh/" + owner + "/" + repo + "/commits"
266		if which == "github" {
267			url = "https://github.com/" + owner + "/" + repo
268		}
269		return openURLCmd(url)
270	}
271	
272	// openURLCmd returns a command that opens url in the default browser without
273	// blocking the UI. A failure is silent — the URL is also shown as an OSC 8 link.
274	func openURLCmd(url string) tea.Cmd {
275		return func() tea.Msg {
276			var name string
277			var args []string
278			switch runtime.GOOS {
279			case "darwin":
280				name, args = "open", []string{url}
281			case "windows":
282				name, args = "rundll32", []string{"url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", url}
283			default:
284				name, args = "xdg-open", []string{url}
285			}
286			_ = exec.Command(name, args...).Start()
287			return nil
288		}
289	}
290	
291	func (m *Model) source() []judge.RunReport {
292		if m.section == sectionExcluded {
293			return m.excluded
294		}
295		return m.ranked
296	}
297	
298	// rebuildVisible recomputes the filtered rows for the active section and refreshes
299	// the table + detail.
300	func (m *Model) rebuildVisible() {
301		q := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m.filter.Value()))
302		m.visible = m.visible[:0]
303		for _, r := range m.source() {
304			if q == "" || strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.SubmissionID), q) {
305				m.visible = append(m.visible, r)
306			}
307		}
308		m.table.SetRows(submissionRows(m.visible, m.section))
309		if m.table.Cursor() >= len(m.visible) {
310			m.table.SetCursor(max(0, len(m.visible)-1))
311		}
312		m.refreshDetail()
313	}
314	
315	func (m *Model) refreshDetail() {
316		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
317			m.vp.SetContent(m.theme.dimStyle().Render("No submissions in this section."))
318			m.vp.GotoTop()
319			return
320		}
321		idx := m.table.Cursor()
322		if idx < 0 || idx >= len(m.visible) {
323			idx = 0
324		}
325		rank := 0
326		if m.section == sectionRanked {
327			rank = idx + 1
328		}
329		content := renderDetail(m.theme, &m.visible[idx], m.meta, m.section == sectionExcluded, rank, m.detailWidth)
330		m.vp.SetContent(content)
331		m.vp.GotoTop()
332	}
333	
334	func (m Model) View() string {
335		if !m.ready {
336			return "loading…"
337		}
338		if len(m.ranked) == 0 && len(m.excluded) == 0 {
339			return "No submissions to display.\n"
340		}
341	
342		// ---- header + tabs/filter (clipped to one line each so the layout math
343		// never drifts) ----
344		clip := lipgloss.NewStyle().MaxWidth(m.width)
345		title := clip.Render(m.theme.titleStyle().Render("entire-judge") +
346			m.theme.dimStyle().Render(fmt.Sprintf("  ·  %d ranked · %d excluded  ·  agent %s",
347				len(m.ranked), len(m.excluded), m.meta.Agent)))
348	
349		var secondRow string
350		if m.filtering {
351			secondRow = clip.Render(m.filter.View())
352		} else {
353			secondRow = clip.Render(m.renderTabs())
354		}
355	
356		// ---- body panes ----
357		leftPane := m.theme.paneStyle(!m.focusDetail).
358			Width(m.leftInner).Height(m.paneContentH).MaxHeight(m.paneContentH + 2).Render(m.table.View())
359		rightPane := m.theme.paneStyle(m.focusDetail).
360			Width(m.rightInner).Height(m.paneContentH).MaxHeight(m.paneContentH + 2).Render(m.vp.View())
361		// Clip the joined body to the terminal width so the two min-width panes can't
362		// overflow (and wrap) on a narrow terminal.
363		body := lipgloss.NewStyle().MaxWidth(m.width).Render(
364			lipgloss.JoinHorizontal(lipgloss.Top, leftPane, rightPane))
365	
366		return strings.Join([]string{title, secondRow, body, m.footerView()}, "\n")
367	}
368	
369	// footerView renders the help line (plus a scroll hint when the detail pane has
370	// more below the fold) and the advisory disclaimer.
371	func (m Model) footerView() string {
372		help := m.help.View(m.keys)
373		if m.focusDetail && !m.vp.AtBottom() {
374			help += m.theme.dimStyle().Render("   ↓ more")
375		}
376		disclaimer := lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(m.theme.Dim).Italic(true).
377			MaxWidth(m.width).Render(judge.Disclaimer)
378		return help + "\n" + disclaimer
379	}
380	
381	func (m Model) renderTabs() string {
382		active := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(m.theme.Accent).Foreground(lipgloss.Color("0")).Bold(true)
383		inactive := m.theme.dimStyle()
384		ranked := fmt.Sprintf(" Ranked (%d) ", len(m.ranked))
385		excluded := fmt.Sprintf(" Excluded (%d) ", len(m.excluded))
386		if m.section == sectionRanked {
387			return active.Render(ranked) + " " + inactive.Render(excluded)
388		}
389		return inactive.Render(ranked) + " " + active.Render(excluded)
390	}
391	
392	// ScoreBar renders a score as a "█████░░ 4.0/5" style bar; an unscored lens shows
393	// a dash bar. It is plain text (no ANSI) so the non-TTY plain renderer can reuse
394	// it; the TUI uses its own colored bar.
395	func ScoreBar(score *float64) string {
396		const cells = 5
397		if score == nil {
398			return strings.Repeat("░", cells) + " -/5"
399		}
400		filled := int(*score + 0.5)
401		if filled < 0 {
402			filled = 0
403		}
404		if filled > cells {
405			filled = cells
406		}
407		return strings.Repeat("█", filled) + strings.Repeat("░", cells-filled) + fmt.Sprintf(" %.1f/5", *score)
408	}
409	
410	// truncate shortens value to at most max display columns, on rune boundaries,
411	// appending an ellipsis when it cuts. It is display-width aware (multi-byte runes
412	// and wide glyphs are measured correctly), so it never splits a UTF-8 rune.
413	func truncate(value string, max int) string {
414		if max <= 0 {
415			return ""
416		}
417		return runewidth.Truncate(value, max, "...")
418	}
